html:
SMTO-LLM-0003 — Model server connection was refused

GUID: 475c7c8d-ea58-446d-9966-5090bbd4d7c9
Slug: llm-connection-refused
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • SMTO reached the computer where the model should be, but nothing there accepted the connection. Usually the model server isn't running or is on a different port.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card and check that Endpoint has the right address and port number. A wrong port number sends SMTO to a place where no model server is listening.
  2. If the model server is one SMTO manages, open the Inference page and make sure it's running. When the model server is stopped, its computer turns the connection away.
  3. Otherwise, ask the person who runs the model server to confirm it's started and accepts connections on that port. Only someone with access to that computer can start the server or open the port.
  4. Select Check saved model on the Main card, then start a new task. A passing check confirms SMTO can now connect before you send real work.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model passes and a new task gets an answer from the model.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the model server's address, to the person who manages the model server. Don't change other settings or turn off security checks to make the connection work.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The TCP connection to the configured model endpoint's host and port was refused (ECONNREFUSED) before any model response.

What this means

  • The network rejected the connection attempt at the configured address and port. This differs from a hostname lookup failure and occurs before an authenticated model response can be assessed. A stopped listener, wrong port or active network rejection are possible; this error alone does not select one.

Why this can happen

  • A listener may be stopped or bound to a different port or interface; a firewall can also actively refuse a connection.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the Model Configuration host and port with the provider listener. Check reachability from the machine making the request, not only from a browser on another computer.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the Endpoint host and port on the role's card in Settings › Setup › Model routing, then verify on that host that the model server is running and listening on that interface and port (for example ss -ltnp, or the managed instance's state on the Inference page). A firewall actively rejecting the port causes the same error.
  • Check the configured model host and port, then ask the provider operator to confirm the model server is running and its listener accepts connections there.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open LLM Endpoint: model-configuration / llm_base_url. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A connection from the requesting machine reaches the intended listener and a model request receives a response.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Typed transport exception (or exact legacy standard reason where supported); no tool outcome is inferred from connection state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
